summary: Round 9 by review_rounds.py's count (rounds 1-2 were the split commit), production. The round-8 major is fixed and I re-measured both directions in my own tree: DEFAULT_SEEDS 1000->10 gives '2 tests completed, 1 failed' at CommitProtocolSweepTest.java:146, and -Dsweep.seeds=10 stays BUILD SUCCESSFUL printing 'sweep: 10 seeds in 507 ms, 840 readers judged'. Unmutated default run: BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 16s, 'sweep: 1000 seeds in 14723 ms, 74172 readers judged' -- 74.17 readers/seed, matching the floor comment's cited figure exactly. Pinning SEEDS rather than DEFAULT_SEEDS also makes all six SEEDS*k floors ABSOLUTE in the unset case, which closes the loop-bound as a side effect: with SEEDS pinned at 1000 the takeovers floor alone bounds the seeds actually swept at >=52% of them. THE BASELINE ENTRY CHECKS OUT AGAINST THE VERDICTS, including the sentence I expected to falsify. Round-by-round against .harness/review: R3 322f180 the violation message asserted only the invariant name and the named mutant survived (and M4.13's own notes had already required asserting its content); R4 28bc2c0 the ack trace omitted every fenced writer while the same file called a zombie 'the ONLY thing that makes I5 reachable'; R5 69c75e7 deleting every acks.add left the suite green; R6 a5f2698 the fix for that, ackFloorAlwaysZero, was a relative assertion an empty trace satisfies; R7 0f062ae the addAll was droppable a second time and the new checkReader test duplicated five existing ones (named in that verdict: four in ReaderInvariantsTest plus ReaderInvariantsScopeTest); R8 aae3b85 the guard sat on the fallback. So 'every round past the cap found an assertion that cannot fail, and each time I had already written down that it could' holds for every one of rounds 3-8. Cost lens: nothing here changes a production request path -- the diff is test scaffolding, one buildSrc property forward, and docs -- and the added per-epoch CommitLog.recover() runs against MemoryBinStore inside the sweep, with M4.13h and M4.24 already owning its O(E-squared) shape. Four minors, none producing a wrong result today.

findings.title: a committed `sweep.seeds` skips the guard entirely, and the only thing stopping it is a javadoc asking the next hand to remember
findings.failure_scenario: The guard is `if (System.getProperty("sweep.seeds") == null)`, and this commit's own buildSrc change is what makes the property reach the test JVM. One line in gradle.properties, or one `-Dsweep.seeds=` in a CI step, and the completion-condition assertion is skipped while all six floors scale down with SEEDS -- so M4's 'I1-I5 hold across 1,000 deterministic seeds' is reported met by a run of one seed, permanently and silently, with the archive row asserting 1,000. MEASURED in my tree: `-Dsweep.seeds=10` is BUILD SUCCESSFUL, tests=2 failures=0, printing 'sweep: 10 seeds in 507 ms'; the round-8 test-reviewer measured the same at 1 seed, 172 ms, 87 readers judged. Lines 81-83 state the hazard in prose ('SETTING THE PROPERTY SKIPS THE WORKLOAD ASSERTION BELOW ... must not be reported as one'), which is the 'remember to' shape gate-design rung 1 exists to replace: whether a committed file sets sweep.seeds is a grep predicate over the tree. M0.89, added by this same diff, guards only the FORWARDING lines against deletion, not the property against being set -- so this residue has no gate and no row.
findings.suggestion: Widen M0.89's grep predicate to also reject `sweep.seeds` appearing in any committed gradle.properties, CI workflow or conventions default -- one added pattern in a check that is already being written -- rather than leaving the javadoc as the control.

findings.title: M4.47 is landed and its row still says `todo`, in a file this diff edits and a tree whose staged notes cite M4.47 as done
findings.failure_scenario: Commit 442020a ('M4.47: seal the burned run') landed ADR-0037; ChainReplay.java carries the change and backlog-done.md has no M4.47 row, so backlog.md:152 still reads '⚠️ I2 IS VIOLATED UNDER FAULT INJECTION ... Implement that. | FR-11, NFR-11 | todo'. An agent running `next-task` picks the highest-signal open row and starts re-implementing work that shipped, against a tree where the fix is already present. The tree now contradicts itself inside one commit: this diff's backlog-notes.md:951 says 'verified by reverting M4.47' and its M4.13e section says 'M4.47's seal-the-run fences a zombie before it can commit', both treating it as landed, while the row three lines from rows this diff edits says it is not. Flagged rather than fixed because fixing it here widens this commit's scope past one task; it belongs in the next commit that touches the backlog.
findings.suggestion: Move the M4.47 row to backlog-done.md in whatever commit lands next, not this one.

findings.title: 'Every violation names the seed that reproduces it' is no longer what the code does, and the archive row is the copy that never gets rewritten
findings.failure_scenario: Round 6 (a5f2698) found the report unbounded -- one line per violation, 2,000 identical lines from 13 seeds -- and the fix at CommitProtocolSweepTest.java:186-190 prints ONE line per failing seed: the first violation plus '(+N more on this seed)'. So on a seed with five violations, four of them appear nowhere and do not name the seed. The archive row and the assertion description at line 258 both still promise 'every violation names the seed that reproduces it'. The criterion's PURPOSE holds -- the seed is what reproduces it, and re-running that seed shows the rest -- but the sentence as written is now inaccurate, and backlog-done.md is by its own header the file that 'never rewrites rows that already shipped', so this is the copy that stays wrong. This is the failure mode backlog-done.md:115 already records for M4.0: a fact updated in one place and left stale in its duplicate.
findings.suggestion: Say what the code does in both places: 'every failing seed is named, with its first violation and the count of the rest' -- and note that suppressing the rest is deliberate, which the code comment already argues.

findings.title: ANSWER TO THE QUESTION ASKED, recorded as evidence and not as a defect: the entry's claims hold, with one compression worth naming
findings.failure_scenario: No failure today; recorded because the entry is the durable record of why this went past the cap and two earlier drafts of a similar entry were falsified. Every enumerated claim checks out against .harness/review: the five duplicated tests, the addAll surviving twice, ackFloorAlwaysZero being satisfied by an empty trace, six SEEDS*k floors green at 1/200th, and the guard landing on the fallback. THE ONE COMPRESSION: 'both reviewers measured a one-token rewrite of the `Integer.getInteger` line green at 10 seeds' is true of both reviewers but not of the same round. The reviewer measured it at round 8 (aae3b85.reviewer.json: line 77 -> `Integer.getInteger("sweep.seeds", 10)`, 'sweep: 10 seeds in 457 ms'), AGAINST the DEFAULT_SEEDS guard. The test reviewer measured that rewrite at round 7 (0f062ae.test-reviewer.json: line 79 -> ..., 10), when there was no guard at all; at round 8 it filed the hole as a MINOR on a PASS verdict and its own mutation field reads 'No source mutation needed: set sweep.seeds=1 in gradle.properties or a CI step'. A reader takes the sentence as two independent measurements against the same guarded file, which is one more than there were. The independent corroboration the sentence is claiming is real -- both roles found the hole from opposite sides -- so this is not the class of error that falsified the earlier drafts.
findings.suggestion: If it is touched at all, attribute the two measurements to their rounds rather than merging them; per this gate's own remedy, deleting the clause is preferable to a third rewrite.
